title: Uniform finite-level bounds of one smooth compact-support composite
statement: Fix a characteristic-p field k, primes ell!=p and a finite extension E/Q_ell. Let X,Y be separated finite-type k-schemes, f:X->Y smooth of pure relative dimension d, and c any fixed compactification of f. Use the specified ordinary tower operations and compactification composite F_c [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. If an actual tower C has the finite-level bounds of [def-sp-chart-tate-tower-data], with independent ordered cohomological and Tor intervals [a,b] and [s,t], then every level of F_c C is intrinsically constructible finite-Tor, has cohomological support in [s,t+2d] and Tor amplitude in [s,t+2d]. This assertion concerns finite-level bounds only, not the full ordinary tower domain.

proof.text: Finite type over the field makes both schemes Noetherian. The Over relation and cancellation of separatedness and local finite type show that the map itself is separated and finite type. Its chosen compactification therefore has the hypotheses of the existing uniform compact-support theorem.

proof.text: Smoothness of relative dimension d survives base change to an algebraic closure of every residue field. The existing topologicalKrullDim_le_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension bound gives geometric fibre dimension at most d, without a closed-point or finite-field hypothesis.

proof.text: Apply compactSupport_uniform_tor_bound [det-sp-tower-bound-uniform]. Its finite-coefficient clause gives constructibility at each level, since R_n is finite and ell^(n+1)=0 in its quotient. Its tower clause gives the required uniform cohomology vanishing and Tor interval [s,t+2d].

proof.text: The compactification evaluation comparison [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels] identifies the tower output with the intrinsic finite open-extension/direct-image composite. Identify its open factor with the constant-ring factor by uniqueness of left adjoints to the normalized inverse-image functor. Transport constructibility, cohomology vanishing and Tor amplitude across these derived isomorphisms. These give exactly bounds, without asserting a tower domain.

theorem smooth_tower_compact_bounds
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharP k p] (hlp : l ≠ p)
    (base : SpTowerShriek.Base l E) (ops : SpTowerShriek.Operations l E base)
    (X Y : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [IsSeparated X.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.hom]
    [IsSeparated Y.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType Y.hom] [QuasiCompact Y.hom]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (d : ℕ) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f.left]
    (c : Compactification f.left) (C : SpTowerShriek.D l E X.left)
    (a b s t : ℤ) (_hab : a ≤ b) (hst : s ≤ t)
    (hC : bounds l E X.left C a b s t) :
    bounds l E Y.left ((SpTowerShriek.F l E base ops c).obj C)
      s (t + 2 * (d : ℤ)) s (t + 2 * (d : ℤ))
